purpose: Hand-authored claims of which theories/<Module>.v are checked, by a differential test, against the ACTUAL shipped production OCaml — not merely against the extracted Rocq model in isolation. This is a distinct question from 'is it proven': every theorem in proof-ledger.json is proven either way. It is the backlog-201 answer to 'model vs production' for this project, made mechanical rather than left to STATUS prose. scripts/check-production-link.py verifies each entry below against the freshly generated ledger and the named test file's real content (production_call must appear as a live reference, comments and string literals stripped).
known_gap: test/test_convergence_live.ml calls the real Sarek_convergence.check_expr directly (positive/negative baseline + F-01/F-02 regressions), but it is a fixed-pattern regression suite, not a differential property comparing its result against ConvergenceSpec/ConvergenceSemantics' extracted model on the same inputs. No module is claimed shipped-linked here for that reason: all 111 theorems in this project are proven about the Rocq model (or QCheck-validated against the extracted OCaml model / extracted operational evaluator eval_concrete), with no mechanical assertion that the model and Sarek_convergence.ml agree on a shared input. Closing this gap would mean extending the differential-testing pattern already used in formal/type-safety (T1-CMBT / T2-UNIFY) to this project's checker.
